  "reasoning": "All 16 selected answers agree with their own captured worked solutions and are mathematically correct. Two authored transcription errors remain: q-119770's concluding equation changes the denominator from 1+sin(x) to 2+sin(x); that concluding equation is false (at x=0 its left side is 1/2). Its preceding derivation correctly establishes the answer 1 for the actual question. q-43298 briefly substitutes theta for t in an intermediate line; its final answer remains correct. Mathematics: q-65249 factors the denominator into cos²(theta)(cos²(theta)+sin²(theta)), giving tan(theta). q-72712 factors sin(x) and uses sin²(x)+cos²(x)=1, giving tan(x)+sec(x). q-119770 uses cos²(x)=(1-sin(x))(1+sin(x)), giving 1. q-43298 expands to cos(t)+sin²(t)/cos(t)=sec(t). These simplifications hold on their original domains. q-1708 and q-65430 use the sine sum and difference formulas to obtain (sqrt(6)+sqrt(2))/4 and (sqrt(6)-sqrt(2))/4. The same formulas give q-141275=-(sin(x)+sqrt(3)cos(x))/2, q-65438=sqrt(2)(sin(x)-cos(x))/2, q-65437=sqrt(2)(sin(x)+cos(x))/2, and q-141284=-cos(x). q-109000 uses the quotient rule, giving v(t)=2t/(t²+1)². q-19299 differentiates to -4e^(-t)+6t-2, so v(2)=10-4e^(-2), rounded to 9.46. q-109012 has velocity -3/t², so speed at t=3 is 1/3 miles/h. Substitution and the power rule give the three antiderivatives: q-113502=-3(2-5x)^6/5+C, q-72424=-(7-2x)^8+C, and q-113509=-1/[2(x-2)²]+C. Differentiating each recovers its integrand. Velocity choice labels v(t)= and v= identify the same quantities computed in the solutions. No submitted grades were supplied; every MA answer below is supported solely by its own captured worked solution.",
